text:
Alex: Quick async standup — kernel + batching + KV cache perf. What I did: landed kernel prefetch patch, ran microbatch perf for seq=512 and saw ~7% median latency drop. Blockers: KV eviction still noisy under bursty fanout; eviction thrash spikes CPU. Today: iterate on eviction policy, run 6h long-tail bench, and pinging @Sam for PR review (#3421).

Priya: Nice. Can you paste the perf numbers (p50/p95/p99 + tokens/s)?

Alex: Sure, ran locally and on staging:
```
# bench command
./bench --model redwood-v2 --seq 512 --batch 16 --iters 200

Staging (no prefetch): p50: 38ms  p95: 85ms  p99: 160ms  tokens/s: 4200
Staging (with prefetch): p50: 35ms  p95: 78ms  p99: 150ms  tokens/s: 4520
```

Sam: I'll take the PR today. For KV eviction, what's the current heuristic? LRU + time decay?

Alex: Right now it's LRU with exponential time decay and a hard size threshold. Eviction thrash appears when a small set of keys become hot briefly and then cold — considering TTL buckets or adaptive decay based on request hotness.

Lin: I can add a bursty-fanout workload to the generator to simulate that pattern. Want me to model N=1000 clients hitting 100 keys with Zipf skew?

Alex: Please do. Zipf with s=1.2 and intermittent 5s bursts should match observed traces. Link to the generator: https://internal.tools/workloads/bench-gen (internal).

Diego: Kicked off long-run on dedicated cluster. Artifacts will land here: s3://redwood-perf/1765509876/ — I'll post logs and flamegraphs when complete.

Maya: :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Build #3421 completed: unit tests ✅, integration tests: kv-eviction-stress failed — rerun queued.

Alex: Thanks. Once CI green I'll push the microbatch config tweak. If anyone spots increased latency in the dashboard (route=redwood-v2, region=us-west-2), tag me and drop console links. Back to async work :)
